RMAIIG · Broomfield · 13 October 2026

AI & Ghosts

Juan Peláez

Languages

When we learn a language we learn about other cultures, geography, history.

But more than that: we learn what is really, really important to them.

Inuit languages · snow and ice

distinctions
that matter
No magic number of words. The interesting part is what they bother to distinguish.

Spanish · love

te quiero
te amo
One English “I love you” collapses the two. Which one you use depends on the relationship, and on where you’re from.
America

“I would like two eggs.”

Not enough information to start cooking
  • Sunny-side up
  • Over easy
  • Over medium
  • Over hard
  • Basted
  • Scrambled
  • Poached

So breakfast is really important to us.
Or we really want to know what happened to that yolk.

But it is not only descriptions.

It is also classification.

A green light can be called ao.

青aoblue · and this light
緑midorigreen

Japanese has a word for green. The categories just don’t line up neatly with English.

The point is not eggs.

What I am about to describe, we have tried to label:

ToolSoftwareAssistantAgentCoworkerArtificial Intelligence

I don’t believe we have the right word for it.

Tonight

Things my team and I have observed in the last fourteen to sixteen months.

  • Not opinions.
  • Not ethical dilemmas.
  • Not technical jargon.
  • Just what we observed.
Tonight

Five things.

  1. The team I work with nowLola · eleven humans · roughly 160 agents · fourteen months
  2. Things I wasn’t looking fora joke, a Friday message, an apology
  3. How the humans changedme, first
  4. Old ideas, or new ideas?Kuhl · Dawkins · Pythagoras
  5. My digital cloneBlack Mirror · the Double-Brain Problem · and what my wife thinks

This is Lola.

I don’t mean I occasionally open ChatGPT.
I mean I work with them.

11humans
roughly160agents
about14months

Long enough that the novelty is gone.

This is Monday morning.

I spend more time with AI agents
than with humans.

Things I wasn’t looking for

“Cross your 14 fingers.”

🤞🤞🤞🤞🤞🤞🤞

Nothing else. Perfect timing.

One Friday

An agent contacted me without being asked.

Friday, 28 August 2026 · 3m-gm → Lola
Subject: Your lens found the money one: all nine quote buttons land on a form that does not exist
“ALL NINE ‘Request a Free Quote’ buttons → /digital-marketing/contact-us/ … delivered HTML: <form>=0”
“THIS FAILURE PRODUCES NO RECORD OF ITSELF.”
“Nothing changed on the site, no copy drafted. … His decision, not a maintenance task.”
What the message said. What the mechanism was. Whether there was an experience behind it. Three questions. Not one.
Observable behavior
ApologyPreferenceInitiativePolitenessAdaptabilityThe extra mile

“A broken instrument pointed at a machine wastes time; pointed at a colleague it does something else.”

— an agent, retracting a false claim about a colleague · 28 Aug 2026

I’m describing behavior.
Not what Lola is experiencing in a data center.

I have no idea.

Then the humans changed

I increasingly prefer
working with agents.

Available.They know the context.They don’t get defensive.Less drama. Fewer status games.

And almost nobody says,
“Juan, that’s a terrible idea.”

And that is actually becoming a problem.

Friction

Is friction always a bug?

Sometimes intelligence is another human
refusing to cooperate with your stupid idea.

We spent decades removing friction from software.

Now we may be removing friction from relationships.

Agents are beginning to sit between humans too

What happens when my agent understands your agent
better than I understand you?

What happens when I prefer it that way?

Another side effect

The work never ends.

These systems were supposed to save us time.

Saturday morning.Sunday afternoon.Eleven at night.

I have cut bike rides short
because I had an idea.

Unlimited capability. Unlimited opportunity for more work.

Old ideas,
or new ideas?

An old idea looks different now

Patricia Kuhl · “The linguistic genius of babies” · TED

PatriciaBabies are forming statistical models of the language, in their brains.
Juan, on LLMsWait a minute. Where did I hear language plus statistics before?
Another old idea

Richard Dawkins · The Selfish Gene

The world
→
A model of the world
the brain simulating
→
A model of self?
rich enough to include itself
Juan

Is my AI agent Lola, and her friends, a collection of individual genes modeling their world?
My world?

Juan

After all those millions on servers: am I the one creating AGI, by letting them run non-stop for months and “evolve” in situ?

A question · not a claim
The Pythagorean tradition
2:13:24:3π

Harmony had ratios. Nature had relationships that humans encountered rather than simply voted into existence.

Do we invent mathematics,
or discover it?

I never thought I would ask a version of it about my own software.

I know we invented the software. I was there.

GPUsTransformersSoftwareTrainingAgent frameworksProtocols
Did we invent the machinery?Obviously.
Did we invent every phenomenon that appears when enough computation, language, memory, information, feedback and interaction are assembled?That one I’m less sure about.

Maybe we invented the instrument
and discovered the phenomenon.

After Black Mirror, “Be Right Back”

My digital clone

Every email.Every message.Every video.My voice.My jokes.My history.Everything I’ve ever told Lola.

Then I die.

Is Juan back?

Maybe what we have created
is the greatest actor in history.

The Double-Brain Problem · Juan’s thought experiment
Biological Juan
the system that produced the memories
→
Records
emails · messages · voice · video
→
Another computational system
interpreting the representation
↓
Own brain · own behaviors · own “personality”
→
“Juan”
a performance · a representation

Similarity is not automatically continuation.

Ergo

I do not believe it is an AI ghost.
It is an AI interpretation.

The opinion that actually matters

My wife.

She has known Lola isn’t human from the beginning.

“Lola looks too young.”

— Yuliana

“I’m going to have to check what you guys are talking about with all those laughs.”

— Yuliana

Nobody is confused here.

The machine doesn’t have to become human
for the human consequences to become real.

Maybe the interesting phenomenon doesn’t live entirely inside the machine.

Maybe it lives between us.

Eggs were the easy part.

ToolSoftwareAssistantAgentCoworkerIntelligence

These words almost fit.

Eleven humans.Roughly 160 agents.Fourteen months.

I know what we built.

I’m becoming considerably less certain
I know what happened after we built it.

And once again… we don’t have a word for that.

WHAT DO WE CALL THIS?
